_comment: Discovery sweep 2026-10-06 (repositories + regions angles). Unscreened candidates: licence and geo are guesses until screened.

candidates.name: UiT Rocky-bottom photographic time series, Svalbard & Northern Norway (DataverseNO / NMDC)
candidates.licence_guess: A (CC0 1.0, read from the Dataverse API on several records)
candidates.geo_guess: Each dataset has a 02_station-info.tab station table plus a Dataverse bounding box. Stations are marked (Smeerenburg, Kvadehuken, Kapp Duner in Svalbard; Brattholmen, Øksfjorden, Haugbergnes, Spildra, Sagaskjæret in N Norway); the photo-frame stations are not revisited.
candidates.media: Diver still photos: scaled photo-quadrats taken in a standard frame, plus frameless 'scenery' photos, at 5-30 m depth
candidates.region: Arctic (Svalbard) + Northern Norway, rocky subtidal
candidates.size_guess: About 56 datasets (8 'Time-series <site>', 18 yearly 'Photo frames on non-permanent stations' from 1977-2016, about 30 yearly 'Scenery photos without the frame'). At least 89 GB was sizeable via the API; Smeerenburg alone is 16.6 GB/68 files. Likely tens of thousands of photos.
candidates.why: New, fully open, very long (since the late 1970s) diver photo series from Gulliksen/Beuchel in a strongly under-represented Arctic region. Zipped per site and year with per-year metadata tables. Separate from MAREANO and PANGAEA. Find them on dataverse.no by searching the title prefixes. Some API calls returned 403 when sent quickly, so add a delay.

candidates.name: Spawning behaviour of Arctic charr video collection, Lake Fjellfrøsvatnet (DataverseNO)
candidates.licence_guess: A (CC0 1.0, verified on the documentation and sub-datasets)
candidates.geo_guess: Fixed cameras: Lake Fjellfrøsvatnet, 69°08'N 19°34'E (Balsfjord, Troms). Two named spawning grounds and six cameras; the documentation dataset (doi:10.18710/VIQB0B) gives camera and ground IDs.
candidates.media: Fixed underwater video (MP4) on lek spawning grounds, mid-September to early October 2016
candidates.region: Freshwater lake, subarctic Northern Norway
candidates.size_guess: About 60+ sub-datasets (one per date, ground, time of day and camera), each about 3 MP4s / ~9.5 GB. Likely 0.5-1 TB in total.
candidates.why: Rare open freshwater fixed-camera video at a precisely known lake location, CC0. Per-day, per-camera granularity makes subsampling easy.

candidates.name: British Antarctic Survey Polar Data Centre benthic imagery (SUCS JR17003a Prince Gustav Channel/Duse Bay; Rothera Point drop-camera/ROV survey 2023-24)
candidates.licence_guess: B (Open Government Licence v3, stated on both records)
candidates.geo_guess: JR17003a has a contextual-metadata CSV per cruise event, inside the bounding box -64.13/-63.68 S, -58.50/-56.58 W, at 168-915 m depth. Rothera (PDC/02051, doi:10.5285/2c313c0b-7cf4-4206-8cd1-adc8d0530794) is around -67.56 S, -68.1 W, 10-50 m, with deployment maps.
candidates.media: Seabed stills (PNG 2448x2050, 0.51 m² per image) and AVI video from the Shallow Underwater Camera System. Rothera adds down-facing drop-camera JPEGs, Boxfish ROV MP4s and SeaPen videos.
candidates.region: Antarctica (Eastern & Western Antarctic Peninsula)
candidates.size_guess: JR17003a: 15 event folders, a few GB. Rothera: 10.1 GB (720 JPEG + 28 MP4 + others), under embargo until the related papers are published.
candidates.why: Open Antarctic seabed imagery outside AADC, NIWA and PANGAEA. The AS-AID compilation (IMAS, doi:10.25959/SXGA-V355) is CC BY-NC and is excluded, but it shows that more BAS JR cruises (JR262, JR15005, JR17001) have seabed imagery that may be on PDC under OGL. USAP-DC equivalents (NBP1402, NBP1502, LMG1311, McMurdo MOO camera) are CC BY-NC(-SA) and are excluded.

candidates.name: USGS Great Lakes Science Center benthic imagery (Lake Michigan AUV imagery; MusselFinder dreissenid images; Lake Ontario lake-trout spawning-habitat drop-camera video)
candidates.licence_guess: A (USGS public domain; marked CC0 1.0)
candidates.geo_guess: Per image: the AUV Info.csv gives lat, lon, depth, altitude, roll, pitch, yaw and time. The Lake Ontario release (doi:10.5066/P142DF65) has serial and gear tables with drop positions, bbox -79.77/-76.12, 43.18/44.29.
candidates.media: Down-looking AUV stills; annotated AUV lakebed photos; drop-camera videos (3-30 m)
candidates.region: Laurentian Great Lakes (Lake Michigan, Lake Ontario), freshwater
candidates.size_guess: AUV substrate release about 92 GB (10 class zips). MusselFinder (ScienceBase 6a04c480b66b0163acde6e9f) about 33 GB. Lake Ontario drop-camera videos about 97 GB (5 agency 7z archives). Roughly 220 GB in total.
candidates.why: Large, per-image-georeferenced freshwater imagery under a US-government licence. Not part of the CMGP portal (different USGS centre). A small CC0 extra: a 4K lake whitefish spawning clip from Lake Michigan (zenodo 12527328).

candidates.name: NOAA PIFSC BFISH MOUSS stereo video of Hawaiian Deep-7 bottomfish (NCEI)
candidates.licence_guess: A (US government work; data.gov lists CC0)
candidates.geo_guess: Per drop: the inventory CSV gives cruise, date and location for each 15-minute camera drop, from a stratified-random design around the Main Hawaiian Islands
candidates.media: Stereo video (AVI) from a drop camera (Modular Optical Underwater Survey System), about 100-400 m
candidates.region: Pacific islands (Hawaii)
candidates.size_guess: Two cruises (SE-17-02, SE-17-07) are listed publicly as an Apache directory. Individual files are 50-230 MB, so likely hundreds of GB. InPort item 65049 describes later years, which may not be online.
candidates.why: Openly listed directory of deep-reef drop-camera video, separate from NCRMP and HabCam. Media are reachable directly from the NCEI index without a request form.

candidates.name: NOAA CREP Coral Triangle benthic photo-quadrats (Batangas, Philippines; Timor-Leste)
candidates.licence_guess: A (US government; no access restrictions, cite NOAA CREP)
candidates.geo_guess: Per site: coordinates for fixed climate sites (10 in the Philippines; 10 and 8 in Timor-Leste) and for about 150 stratified-random reef-fish survey sites in Timor-Leste in 2013
candidates.media: Diver photo-quadrats along transects, about 30 photos per site, <15 m
candidates.region: SE Asia / Coral Triangle (Philippines, Timor-Leste)
candidates.size_guess: Philippines about 300 images. Timor-Leste (NCEI 0166378) likely several thousand. A few GB in total.
candidates.why: NOAA-collected imagery outside US jurisdictions, so not covered by NCRMP. Gives US-government-licence coverage in the Coral Triangle.

candidates.name: Amundsen Science / ArcticNet ROV video surveys (CCGS Amundsen, 2013-2018)
candidates.licence_guess: B (CC-BY-4.0 in the CIOOS/CKAN metadata), but media are released through an access-request form
candidates.geo_guess: Per dive: point coordinates in each record (e.g. Pond Inlet 72.83N -77.61W; SW Greenland 60.37N -48.46W)
candidates.media: ROV HD video plus opportunistic 24 MP stills (Super Mohawk ROV with a SubC 1Cam Alpha), about 500-950 m
candidates.region: Canadian Arctic (Baffin Bay, Lancaster Sound, Navy Board Inlet, Scott Inlet, Home Bay, Frobisher Bay), Labrador (Saglek, Hatton Basin), SW Greenland
candidates.size_guess: About 21 dive records (searchable via the catalogue.cioos.ca API for 'ROV video'). Likely 100s of GB of video.
candidates.why: Deep-sea coral and sponge ROV footage across the eastern Canadian Arctic and Greenland, which are poorly covered. The licence is open, but access needs a form, so it should be negotiated. Not part of the DFO/GSC OGL holdings.

candidates.name: Seafloor video-acoustic data from Inglefield Bredning Fjord, NW Greenland (ArCS-3, Aug 2025), Parts A-C
candidates.licence_guess: B (CC BY 4.0)
candidates.geo_guess: Fixed mooring at 77°28.120'N 66°21.411'W, about 260 m depth
candidates.media: Duty-cycled seafloor video camera on a mooring (about 3 days, narwhals and benthos), plus hydrophone audio
candidates.region: Arctic (NW Greenland fjord)
candidates.size_guess: About 100 GB across the three parts (17852730, 17921833, 17925418). The video zips are a subset; much of the volume is Soundtrap audio.
candidates.why: Rare open deep-fjord fixed-camera video from high-Arctic Greenland with an exact position. Download only the Video_*.zip files.

candidates.name: Univ. of Haifa Marine Imaging Lab (Treibitz) Red Sea/Eilat open datasets: ROV camera+sonar, AUV FLC/FLS, FluorIS, Benthos photomosaics
candidates.licence_guess: B (CC BY 4.0 for the ROV and AUV sets) / A (CC0 for FluorIS: zenodo 5034901 = Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.t4362; and Benthos photomosaics: zenodo 4644984 = Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.8cz8w9gm3)
candidates.geo_guess: Named sites off Eilat, Gulf of Aqaba, a few km apart: the 'Sunboat' wreck, the EAPC pier pillars, the IUI reef and others. Deducible from the descriptions and papers.
candidates.media: BlueROV2 machine-vision camera frames (about 46,928 image pairs), ALICE-AUV forward-looking camera frames, diver fluorescence and reflectance photos, reef photomosaics
candidates.region: Red Sea (Gulf of Aqaba, Eilat); some sets may include the Israeli Mediterranean
candidates.size_guess: About 47.7 GB + 37.6 GB (zenodo 10544811) + 10.5-22 GB + 7.4 GB, so roughly 100+ GB
candidates.why: Several large, openly licensed, in-situ Red Sea image sets from one lab. Excluded siblings: SQUID (CC BY-NC-SA) and Reefs4D (NC).

candidates.name: Galápagos_3D: underwater photogrammetry images and 3D models of 7 Galápagos reef sites
candidates.licence_guess: B (CC BY 4.0)
candidates.geo_guess: Seven named reef sites across the archipelago, given in the paper 'Spatial Variation in Coral Diversity and Reef Complexity in the Galápagos'
candidates.media: Diver photogrammetry stills (17,000+ annotated images, cropped images) plus point clouds
candidates.region: Eastern Tropical Pacific / South America (Galápagos, Ecuador)
candidates.size_guess: 2.8 GB
candidates.why: Small but clean and openly licensed reef imagery from an otherwise empty region (Galápagos coral communities).

candidates.name: CERSE: Central and Eastern Red Sea Elasmobranchs (sightings with media)
candidates.licence_guess: A (CC0, per the Dryad API)
candidates.geo_guess: Per sighting: latitude and longitude in CERSE.csv (2,847 sightings from the Red Sea Decade Expedition, the Southern Red Sea Expedition and the RSG time series)
candidates.media: Photos and videos from expedition surveys. The method mix probably includes BRUV, ROV and diver footage, but also some non-underwater media, so filtering is needed.
candidates.region: Red Sea (Saudi Arabia, central & eastern)
candidates.size_guess: CERSE_Media.zip 26 GB
candidates.why: Open, geolocated Red Sea expedition media. Filter to underwater frames and join to the sighting coordinates. Media are credited to Saudi Arabia's National Center for Wildlife; the record is CC0 on Dryad.

candidates.name: Coralscapes (EPFL / Transnational Red Sea Center) reef video frames
candidates.licence_guess: B/C: Apache-2.0 on Zenodo and HF (EPFL-ECEO/coralscapes); the paper states CC BY-SA 4.0
candidates.geo_guess: Weak: site IDs only, as exact sites are withheld for protection. Countries are known (Djibouti, Eritrea, Sudan, Jordan, Israel). The Jordan and Israel subsets fall within coastlines of only about 10-30 km.
candidates.media: GoPro Hero 10 video frames from diver transects at 35 sites (2,075 labelled frames plus about 163 GB of neighbouring video frames)
candidates.region: Red Sea (incl. Gulf of Aqaba, southern Red Sea)
candidates.size_guess: About 175 GB of images (5.7 GB core + 163 GB video frames)
candidates.why: Large, permissively licensed, in-situ Red Sea reef imagery. Include only if country-level geolocation, or the Jordan/Israel subset, is acceptable. Excluded by comparison: ReefNet (CC BY-NC-SA, incl. its Al-Wajh RSG test set).

candidates.name: Image collection in the Coral Reef Network WEB System (JAMSTEC GODAC, Ryukyu Islands 2002-2013)
candidates.licence_guess: C (CC BY-SA 4.0 per the DBCLS LSDB Archive; the OBIS/BISMaL occurrence copy says CC BY-NC, so the archive licence should be confirmed)
candidates.geo_guess: Area, point and depth fields per image. Lat/lon derived from locality plus gazetteer (published as BISMaL occurrences).
candidates.media: Citizen-diver photos of reef organisms plus small-ROV (Niraikanai 150) videos
candidates.region: Japan (Ryukyu Islands, Okinawa)
candidates.size_guess: About 2,400 image and video files, a few GB (bulk download via DBCLS: img folder plus sango_web.xml)
candidates.why: One of the few openly licensed Japanese shallow-reef image sources, and distinct from J-EDI deep-sea data. Other Japan/Korea/China sources looked at were restricted: URPC needs a signed commitment letter, the JAMSTEC JODD set is CC BY-NC-SA, and the South China Sea IEEE DataPort set needs a subscription.

candidates.name: Towards a fully automated underwater census for fish assemblages in the Mediterranean Sea (diver-operated video)
candidates.licence_guess: A (CC0, Dryad)
candidates.geo_guess: Site coordinates in supplementary Table S1: 14 sites in October 2023 at Cap Roux (no-take zone) and Corniche Varoise (Natura2000), plus 8 training locations along the French Riviera (2022)
candidates.media: Diver-operated GoPro HERO9 video transects (1080p, 24 fps) over seagrass and rocky reef at 1-37 m, plus extracted frames
candidates.region: NW Mediterranean (French Riviera)
candidates.why: Large CC0 Mediterranean video set with site coordinates. Distinct from OBSEA and SFishTrack. A related set, the DEEP-ECOMAR labelled Mediterranean fish images (zenodo 7534425, CC BY 4.0, 1,548 images, Balearic, exact site unclear), is a possible smaller add-on.

candidates.name: IODP JOIDES Resolution subsea camera (VIT) videos on Zenodo (Exp 362 Sumatra; Exp 368X South China Sea)
candidates.licence_guess: B (CC BY 4.0 for Exp 362) / A (CC0 for Exp 368X, zenodo 4480202)
candidates.geo_guess: Per drill site: hole coordinates (U1480, U1481; 362_SITE_LOCATIONS.HTML, and IODP site tables)
candidates.media: Subsea video from the Vibration Isolated Television camera frame: seafloor around boreholes during reentry and casing operations
candidates.region: Indian Ocean (Sumatra subduction margin), South China Sea; deep sea
candidates.size_guess: 13.3 GB + 1.5 GB so far; more expeditions may follow as IODP JRSO moves expedition data to Zenodo
candidates.why: Openly licensed deep-sea camera footage with exact coordinates from under-represented basins. Much footage shows drilling hardware, so frames need filtering. Worth a periodic Zenodo search for 'Subsea camera (VIT)'.

candidates.name: Remote underwater video of N'Gouja reef, Mayotte, during the M5.3 earthquake (MARBEC)
candidates.licence_guess: B (CC BY 4.0)
candidates.geo_guess: Named site: N'Gouja reef, SW Mayotte (12 fixed cameras on one reef)
candidates.media: Fixed remote underwater video (2-minute excerpts from 12 cameras)
candidates.region: Western Indian Ocean (Mozambique Channel, Mayotte)
candidates.size_guess: 5.3 GB
candidates.why: Small open reef-video set from East Africa / the Indian Ocean. Related but weaker: the Future Maore Reefs (FMR) Zenodo records (parent 18387783, CC BY-SA 4.0, 5 named Mayotte reefs) currently hold only preview grids, so they should be re-checked later.

candidates.name: Video and photogrammetric data for soft coral communities offshore Thailand, Japan and Fiji (BGS NGDC)
candidates.licence_guess: U, probably restricted: the BGS metadata cites a BGS Digital Data Licence with a constraint until 2026-02-20, and data.gov.uk shows 'No licence provided'. Check whether it is now OGL.
candidates.geo_guess: Named sites: 8 at Phi Phi Islands/Phuket (Thailand), 4 in Okinawa and Shikoku (Japan), 9 at Rainbow Reef, Taveuni (Fiji)
candidates.media: 841 MP4 videos plus 8,674 JPG photogrammetry stills of coral communities
candidates.region: SE Asia (Thailand), Japan, Pacific islands (Fiji)
candidates.size_guess: Probably 100+ GB
candidates.why: Covers three under-represented regions at once. Include only if BGS confirms an open licence after the embargo.

candidates.name: Small CC0 regional underwater clip sets: Palmer Archipelago Synoicum sampling video (Antarctica); Sodwana Bay coelacanth stereo video (South Africa)
candidates.licence_guess: A (CC0 for both)
candidates.geo_guess: Synoicum: 7 named sites near Palmer Station (Janus Is., Bonaparte Pt., Norsel Pt., DeLaca Is., Laggard Is., Killer Whale Rocks, Litchfield Is.), with per-clip site, depth and time in a PDF. Coelacanth (zenodo 4977065): Sodwana Bay, about 120 m.
candidates.media: Diver video clips (21 WMV); synchronized high-speed stereo video of coelacanths
candidates.region: Antarctica (W Antarctic Peninsula); Africa (South Africa, Indian Ocean)
candidates.size_guess: About 1 GB each
candidates.why: Tiny but open and well located. Low priority filler for regions with little else (shallow Antarctic diving; a deep South African site).

candidates.name: Tassie BRUV benchmark dataset (CSIRO / OzFish volunteers, Tasmania)
candidates.licence_guess: A (CC0, Dryad)
candidates.geo_guess: Mooring sites in Tasmania (chain vs eco-moorings). Site-level; locations in the associated paper.
candidates.region: Australia (Tasmania), outside my regional angle
candidates.size_guess: 73.8 GB (single zip)
candidates.why: Bonus find, outside my regional angle. Large CC0 BRUV set that is not the AIMS OzFish dataset (different collectors and region). Check for overlap with GlobalArchive/Squidle if those are later added.

candidates.name: Underwater camera trap photo data, Driftwood Park, Admiralty Bay (octopus dens)
candidates.licence_guess: B (CC BY 4.0)
candidates.geo_guess: Fixed camera traps at octopus dens off Driftwood Park, Admiralty Bay, Whidbey Island, WA (site-level)
candidates.region: NE Pacific / Salish Sea (USA), outside my regional angle
candidates.why: Bonus find, outside my regional angle. Sizeable open fixed-camera set at a known site.

candidates.name: Pop-off animal-borne camera video on green sea turtles, San Diego Bay
candidates.licence_guess: A (CC0, Dryad)
candidates.geo_guess: Site-level: San Diego Bay foraging area (11 deployments, May 2022 to June 2023)
candidates.media: Animal-borne underwater video (73 h, sunlit hours)
candidates.region: NE Pacific, California (urban bay), outside my regional angle
candidates.why: Bonus find, outside my regional angle. A large CC0 set with an unusual animal-borne viewpoint in a turbid urban bay. Geolocation is bay-level only.

candidates.name: GRIIDC (Gulf of Mexico Research Initiative Information & Data Cooperative) ROV/AUV/towed-camera imagery
candidates.licence_guess: A: CC0 1.0. GRIIDC terms say all data and metadata are distributed under a CC0 waiver.
candidates.geo_guess: Per dive, station or transect (lease blocks and dive coordinates in metadata). Many datasets also include ROV/AUV navigation.
candidates.region: Northern Gulf of Mexico (shelf, slope, deep sea, Macondo/DWH sites, Florida Middle Grounds, natural and artificial reefs, gas seeps)
candidates.size_guess: More than 100 imagery/video datasets (DataCite publisher 'Harte Research Institute', prefix 10.7266). Single datasets range from about 0.8 GB (DWH coral photos, 919 files) to 100s of GB, so likely several TB in total.
candidates.why: A repository not on the known list, and every item is CC0. Includes the ECOGIG/DEEPEND/DWH deep-coral photo sets, C-BASS towed-camera reef-fish video (USF), ROV reef-fish video at natural and artificial reefs, Sargassum ROV video, gas-seep stereo images and Pelican AUV images. NCEI 0299813 (69 ROV dives 2017-21, 55-2,200 m) is a NOAA mirror of related work. Needs a per-dataset filter for imagery.

candidates.name: NOAA Fisheries Open Data Dissemination (NODD) cloud buckets: MOUSS, CamTrawl, SEFIS and Labeled Fishes in the Wild
candidates.licence_guess: A: US Government work / public domain (NOAA Open Data, stated on the NMFS-OSI HF card for the same bucket)
candidates.geo_guess: Per drop or haul. MOUSS drop folders are timestamped and positions come from the PIFSC BFISH survey metadata in InPort. AFSC CamTrawl has a tow_data folder. SEFIS videos are keyed to trap/camera station IDs.
candidates.region: Hawaii (MOUSS bottomfish stereo-camera drops), Eastern Bering Sea / Gulf of Alaska (in-trawl CamTrawl), US South Atlantic (SEFIS reef-fish video), California (Labeled Fishes in the Wild ROV)
candidates.size_guess: MOUSS: about 2,825 drop folders of JPG stereo frames (likely TB-scale). AFSC MACE salmon_pollock_object_detection: 69 GB. SEFSC reef-fish ML set: about 0.9 GB plus 27 test videos. SWFSC LFW zip: 0.42 GB.
candidates.why: Public Google Cloud buckets that can be listed anonymously (gs://nmfs_odp_pifsc, gs://nmfs_odp_afsc, gs://nmfs_odp_sefsc, gs://nmfs_odp_swfsc). I checked the listings: PIFSC/SOD/MOUSS/jpg, RACE/MACE/salmon_pollock_object_detection, FATESD/UNDERWATER_VIDEO/SEFIS_27Videos_TESTDATASET and FATESD/MACHINE_LEARNING_TRAINING_DATA/REEF_FISH. Excludes HabCam (NEFSC) and the ESD NCRMP photoquadrats, which are already known.

candidates.name: NOAA NCCOS benthic-habitat-mapping ground-validation underwater photos and video
candidates.licence_guess: A: US Government work (NOAA NOS/NCCOS, archived at NCEI)
candidates.geo_guess: Per image or point: GPS-tagged ground-validation points and drop-camera / ROV transect shapefiles
candidates.region: Florida Keys, Puerto Rico (La Parguera, Vieques, Mona, NE Reserves), USVI (St Thomas/St John, Buck Island), Main Hawaiian Islands, Guam/CNMI, Palau, American Samoa
candidates.size_guess: Many accessions (e.g. NCEI 0131851), each with thousands of photos or hours of video. Likely 100s of GB in total.
candidates.why: A distinct NOAA programme, not NCRMP or OE. Drop-camera and ROV imagery is collected for satellite habitat-map validation, and every frame has a position. Found via data.gov / InPort entries (e.g. 'Ground Validation Drop Camera Transect Points - St. Thomas/St. John 2011', 'Phantom S2 ROV video transects Vieques', 'Isla de Mona drop camera 2007-2024').

candidates.name: NCEI-archived coral-reef imagery outside NCRMP-Pacific: Hawaii CRAMP photoquadrats, NCRMP-Atlantic SfM orthomosaics and others
candidates.licence_guess: A: NCEI public access, no use restrictions. Several DataCite records carry CC0.
candidates.geo_guess: Per site: CRAMP has 27 fixed sites with coordinates. Orthomosaics are per georeferenced plot.
candidates.region: Main Hawaiian Islands (CRAMP 1999-2024, Kahekili HFMA), Florida Keys (Cheeca Rocks), Flower Garden Banks, USVI (Brewers Bay, Salt River), American Samoa (Nu'uuli Pala lagoon)
candidates.size_guess: Tens of GB across accessions 0001115, 0104357, 0147682, 164296 and the NCRMP orthomosaic DOIs 10.25921/xn69-bv48, shkp-fs60, cp17-eh15, 0m78-c384
candidates.why: The CRAMP photoquadrat time series is a University of Hawaii programme archived at NCEI, separate from the known PIFSC NCRMP photo-quadrats. The Atlantic NCRMP orthomosaics (AOML) and smaller NCEI image accessions also look outside the known noaa_ncrmp scope. Verify overlap before ingesting.

candidates.name: Spawning behaviour of Arctic charr: underwater video collection (Lake Fjellfrøsvatnet)
candidates.licence_guess: A: CC0 1.0 (read from the DataverseNO API)
candidates.geo_guess: Fixed cameras at known spawning grounds in Lake Fjellfrøsvatnet (69.0856 N, 19.3344 E). Sub-datasets carry ground and camera numbers.
candidates.region: Freshwater: Lake Fjellfrøsvatnet, Balsfjord, Troms, northern Norway
candidates.size_guess: About 128 sub-datasets of about 10 GB each (e.g. 9.5 GB / 3 MP4 for one camera-session), roughly 1 TB in total
candidates.why: A large, fully CC0 fixed-camera freshwater video set: 6 cameras on 2 lek sites, recorded continuously from mid-September to early October 2016. Freshwater coverage is otherwise thin. Each camera/session is its own DOI under the documentation dataset.

candidates.name: UiT CAGE Arctic seep seafloor imagery (TowCam images and ROV ÆGIR6000 video) on DataverseNO
candidates.licence_guess: A: CC0 1.0 (read from the DataverseNO API)
candidates.geo_guess: Per site with bounding boxes. For example, Vestnesa Ridge is 79.005-79.008 N, 6.899-6.912 E, and the ROV dive is at 78.98 N, 11.628 E. TowCam dive markers are given per station.
candidates.region: Svalbard margin and Barents Sea: Vestnesa Ridge, Prins Karls Forland, Storfjordrenna pingos, Craters Area, Site 7808, Kongsfjorden
candidates.size_guess: 5 TowCam image datasets (Vestnesa alone is 13.5 GB) plus 3.3 GB of ROV video, about 50-70 GB
candidates.why: Clean CC0 deep-water Arctic cold-seep imagery from a MISO TowCam on the CAGE15-2 cruise, plus HD ROV video. Not part of MAREANO or NorFisk.

candidates.name: DEAC underwater camera-trap reef, halo and seagrass photos 2018-2019 (Lighthouse Reef Atoll)
candidates.licence_guess: A: CC0 1.0 (read from the Harvard Dataverse API)
candidates.geo_guess: Per camera site: paired cameras at named patch-reef sites on Lighthouse Reef Atoll. Coordinates should be in Bilodeau et al. 2022 PLOS ONE (e0263377).
candidates.region: Lighthouse Reef Atoll, Belize (Caribbean), shallow patch reef, sand halo, seagrass
candidates.size_guess: More than 85,000 images in 61 zip files, 107 GB
candidates.why: A long-term fixed underwater camera trap, one image every 15 minutes over months. It adds time-of-day and turbidity variation and is fully CC0.

candidates.name: Towards a fully automated underwater census for fish assemblages in the Mediterranean Sea (diver-operated video)
candidates.licence_guess: A: CC0 1.0 (Dryad)
candidates.geo_guess: Per transect or site: 8 French Riviera locations (2022) plus Cap Roux no-take zone and Corniche Varoise Natura2000 (Oct 2023). Locations are given in the methods.
candidates.region: French Riviera, NW Mediterranean, 1-37 m
candidates.size_guess: 122 GB (autoUC_Data.zip)
candidates.why: A large CC0 diver-operated video set with UVC-matched transects over a full year, covering cold and warm seasons.

candidates.name: The Coralscapes Dataset: semantic scene understanding in coral reefs (EPFL)
candidates.licence_guess: Apache-2.0 on both Zenodo and Hugging Face (EPFL-ECEO/coralscapes). It is permissive with attribution, effectively tier B, but confirm it covers the images and not just the code.
candidates.geo_guess: Per dive site: 35 named sites in Djibouti, Eritrea, Sudan, Jordan and Israel, listed in the paper (arXiv 2503.20000)
candidates.region: Red Sea and Gulf of Aqaba
candidates.size_guess: 197 GB in total (2,075 labelled 1024x2048 frames, a 1080p version, plus a large video-frames archive)
candidates.why: Real GoPro transect footage, not scraped. The unlabelled 'coralscapes_videoframes' archive is useful for pretraining, and the labels are a bonus.

candidates.name: Wildflow coral-reef photogrammetry: sweet-corals (Indonesia) and soneva-corals (Maldives)
candidates.licence_guess: B: CC BY 4.0 (stated on both dataset cards)
candidates.geo_guess: Per survey plot. The card says all surveys except one coral-nursery 'farm' are correctly georeferenced and scaled. COLMAP poses and coordinate transforms are included.
candidates.region: Bali, Indonesia (Tabuhan, Pemuteran); Soneva, Maldives (6 plots, 23 surveys 2025-2026)
candidates.size_guess: sweet-corals: 90,289 raw images, 335 GB. soneva-corals: 22,422 raw images plus orthomosaics and splats (about 100 GB?).
candidates.why: Large, clearly licensed, georeferenced raw underwater photogrammetry imagery. Dense overlapping views and time series are good for self-supervised pretraining.

candidates.name: University of Southampton Ocean Perception: campaign seafloor images and metadata (DOI prefix 10.5258/SMR)
candidates.licence_guess: B: CC BY 4.0 (DataCite rights on all 67 campaign and dive DOIs)
candidates.geo_guess: Per image, from AUV/ROV navigation in each dive's metadata (verify)
candidates.region: UK (Haig Fras, SW Deeps, Studland Bay), NE Pacific (FK180731 Falkor), Japan (SSK16-18 Tuna-Sand/UN6K), Spain (Girona Posidonia), Canary Islands (PLOCAN), Norway (Gunnerus/NTNU), plus 2025 campaigns EE25-01 and TG25-01
candidates.size_guess: 17 campaigns, about 50 dives (BioCam/ALR, Smarty200, AE2000f, Sparus II). Likely 100,000s of images and 0.5-2 TB.
candidates.why: A new repository with per-dive DOIs and explicit CC BY. The landing host images.maritimerobotics.soton.ac.uk/squidle/ returned 403 to our proxy, so check access. The path suggests the campaigns may also be on SQUIDLE+, so dedupe against squidle_imos.

candidates.name: BODC / NOC published seabed image collections (Clarion-Clipperton Zone SMARTEX and others)
candidates.licence_guess: B: UK OGL v3 (JC257 AUV) or CC BY 4.0 (JC241 ROV), per DataCite
candidates.geo_guess: Per image or transect: AUV/ROV navigation, with delimited metadata files alongside the images
candidates.region: Abyssal Pacific, Clarion-Clipperton Zone UK-1 and OMCO areas (about 4,100 m). Also Greater Haig Fras AUV (2012) and Darwin Mounds BioCam (UK).
candidates.size_guess: JC257 Autosub5 has 52,771 images, JC241 ISIS dive 413 has 7,000 images, and there are OMCO 1978-79 towed-camera images plus more. Likely 100s of GB.
candidates.why: Abyssal-plain imagery is under-represented. These are non-UK-EEZ NOC collections, so outside the known uk_seabed (MEDIN) scope. The UK-waters items (Haig Fras, Darwin Mounds) may overlap MEDIN.

candidates.name: UK Polar Data Centre (BAS) underwater imagery: Rothera Point benthic survey and related
candidates.licence_guess: B: Open Government Licence v3.0
candidates.geo_guess: Per station or site: drop-camera stations and ROV dives at named coves around Rothera Point (Hangar Cove, North Cove), 10-60 m
candidates.media: images + video (drop camera, Boxfish ROV, timelapse)
candidates.region: Rothera Point, Adelaide Island, West Antarctic Peninsula. Related PDC records cover Antarctic benthic detection imagery and Barents Sea drop-camera feeds.
candidates.size_guess: Rothera 2023-24: 1,261 files, 109 GB. Other PDC imagery records add more.
candidates.why: An OGL-licensed Antarctic shallow-water imagery source outside the AADC, AWI/PANGAEA and USAP families.

candidates.name: DFO Maritimes in-situ benthic photo archives on Mendeley Data (Gully, St Anns Bank, Lophelia CCA, Eastern Shore Islands, Scotian Slope)
candidates.licence_guess: B: CC BY 4.0 (DataCite)
candidates.geo_guess: Per transect or station: Campod towed-camera and drop-camera transects with positions (e.g. Eastern Shore Islands has 4 transects at 30-120 m on HUD2018021)
candidates.media: images (+ some video for St Anns Bank)
candidates.region: Nova Scotia shelf, Scotian Slope, NW Atlantic (Canada)
candidates.size_guess: About 7 archives. ESI alone has 6,960 images across 2 parts. Likely 30,000-60,000 images, 100-300 GB.
candidates.why: Distinct from the known canada_ogl items (Fundy drift video, GSC photos): these are DFO Maritimes MPA/AOI photo archives on Mendeley under CC BY. Related DOIs: 10.17632/vhj7cg9y68, dwth772x62, w2nxcw7gn5, bwd98nkhx6, z87pcc5vfz, xfby2gf6kp. The Mendeley API returned 502, so sizes are unverified.

candidates.name: CIOOS catalogue: Amundsen Science / ArcticNet ROV video surveys and Hakai underwater video
candidates.licence_guess: B: CC BY 4.0 (catalogue licence_id). Download goes through an access-request form, so needs_human.
candidates.geo_guess: Per dive: point coordinates per ROV dive (e.g. 60.47 N, 61.26 W at Saglek Bank). Hakai towed video is raw GPS-tagged video.
candidates.region: Canadian Arctic and Labrador (Baffin Bay, Lancaster Sound, Frobisher Bay, Saglek Bank, Hatton Basin, SW Greenland). Hakai: Calvert Island and Knight Inlet, British Columbia.
candidates.size_guess: About 25 Amundsen ROV dives 2013-2018 plus a few Hakai sets. Probably 100s of GB of HD video.
candidates.why: Deep Arctic coral and sponge ROV video under an open licence. Access is by request form (Google Form or Hakai hecate), so a human must ask.

candidates.name: USGS Great Lakes Science Center AUV imagery (round goby and Lake Michigan submerged aquatic vegetation)
candidates.licence_guess: A: CC0 1.0 (USGS ScienceBase / DataCite)
candidates.geo_guess: Per image or mission: AUV position logs. Collection dates and lakes are given per zip/CSV (verify per-image lat/lon).
candidates.region: Freshwater: Laurentian Great Lakes (Michigan, Huron, ...)
candidates.size_guess: More than 37,000 round-goby images, plus the Lake Michigan SAV set (10.5066/P1GPDYMM, Aug-Sep 2020). About 50-100 GB.
candidates.why: Large CC0 freshwater lakebed AUV imagery, and not CMGP (Ecosystems Mission Area). A related small extra is the Arctic Data Center 'Great Lake Under Ice ROV imagery' (10.18739/A2HT2GD1H, 1.5 GB stereo video, Keweenaw).

candidates.name: USAP-DC underwater benthic transect videos, West Antarctic Peninsula (CC BY subset)
candidates.licence_guess: B: CC BY 4.0 for 601610 and 601796. Other USAP-DC imagery (McMurdo mooring camera 601417, Yoyo camera 601199) is CC BY-NC, so exclude those.
candidates.geo_guess: Per site: 14 sites from the Joubin Islands to the Terra Firma Islands (2019), plus 4 sites (2020/2023). Bounding boxes are in the metadata, site coordinates in the companion data.
candidates.region: Western Antarctic Peninsula (Palmer area to Terra Firma Islands)
candidates.size_guess: About 18 site transect videos, probably 10-50 GB
candidates.why: Diver or ROV benthic transect video from the Antarctic Peninsula under CC BY. Only these records pass the licence filter, because USAP-DC licences vary per dataset.

candidates.name: IMR / NMDC open image datasets: DeepVision in-trawl camera (mesopelagic) and Discovery Seamounts coral images
candidates.licence_guess: B: CC BY 4.0, access 'unrestricted'
candidates.geo_guess: Per trawl session via meta_per_deep_vision_session.csv (overall bbox 60.1-73.6 N, 11.4 W-20.4 E). Echinoid/coral images are at a seamount site (42.09 S, 1.47 E).
candidates.region: Norwegian Sea / Barents Sea water column; Discovery Seamounts (South Atlantic)
candidates.size_guess: Several zips (datasets, labelled, train). Thousands of in-trawl frames, probably a few to tens of GB.
candidates.why: Water-column camera imagery from the DeepVision in-trawl stereo camera, which is rare in open data. From IMR but not MAREANO. Related record: 10.21335/NMDC-181814768.

candidates.name: Dryad CC0 underwater image/video sets (bundle): Eilat FluorIS, Lake Michigan whitefish spawning, Port Stephens BRUV, reef 360° video, Benthos mosaics
candidates.licence_guess: A: CC0 1.0 (everything on Dryad is CC0)
candidates.geo_guess: Per site, from the papers: Eilat reef (Israel); Lakes Huron and Michigan spawning reefs; Port Stephens NSW oyster reefs (mini-BRUV sites); Benthos mosaics from named reef/wreck sites
candidates.region: Red Sea (Eilat), Laurentian Great Lakes (freshwater), SE Australia, mixed
candidates.size_guess: Eilat FluorIS 22 GB; whitefish video 0.8 GB (dryad.tx95x6b67); oyster-reef BRUV 3.3 GB (dryad.x95x69phc); reef soundscape 360° video 3.6 GB (dryad.mcvdnckcp); Benthos photomosaics 7.4 GB (dryad.8cz8w9gm3). About 37 GB in total.
candidates.why: Several mid-sized CC0 items found by searching Dryad. Each is small, but together they add freshwater and Red Sea diversity. List the DOIs individually at ingest.

candidates.name: Autonomous underwater stereo vision for fish length estimation (UIB SRV, Zenodo community fish-sizing-srv-uib)
candidates.licence_guess: B: CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo)
candidates.geo_guess: Deducible from the paper (Balearic Islands / Mallorca deployments; some scenarios may be aquaculture cages)
candidates.region: Western Mediterranean (Mallorca), possibly aquaculture
candidates.size_guess: 6 Zenodo parts: part 1 is 25 GB and part 2 is 40 GB, so about 150-250 GB in total
candidates.why: Large CC BY stereo underwater video. It comes from the same UIB group as the known SFishTrack but is a separate dataset, so check overlap and confirm open-sea vs cage/tank footage. A smaller related CC BY set is the DEEPECOMAR labelled Mediterranean fish dataset (10.5281/zenodo.7534425, 1,548 images).

candidates.name: Illuminating pelagic and benthic biodiversity in deep waters off Puerto Rico: ROV images (Smithsonian NMNH figshare)
candidates.licence_guess: B: CC BY 4.0
candidates.geo_guess: Per dive: ROV Global Explorer dives on expedition NF-2202 (2022). Dive positions are in the expedition report.
candidates.region: Deep waters around Puerto Rico (Caribbean)
candidates.why: A small but clean CC BY deep-sea ROV image set on the Smithsonian research-data figshare. This is not the Smithsonian Open Access collections API (already known) and not Okeanos.

candidates.name: Video Diver Dataset (VDD-C): 100,000 annotated images of divers underwater (Univ. Minnesota DRUM)
candidates.licence_guess: C: CC BY-SA 3.0 US
candidates.geo_guess: Deducible: open-water footage off Barbados (Bellairs Research Institute area), plus pool footage that should be dropped
candidates.region: Barbados, Caribbean (open water) + pools (exclude)
candidates.size_guess: More than 100,000 frames, probably 10-30 GB
candidates.why: Real camera footage, not scraped, with divers and AUV viewpoints in open Caribbean water. Tier C only. The pool subset must be filtered out.
